          Work with us

          Resilience is built, not measured

          This portal is the diagnostic layer of Think City’s 4D approach — a data-driven, community-first method for regenerating places. It brings together resilience scoring, demographic profiling and spatial analysis so that every stage of a project starts from evidence, not assumption.

          Talk to Think City →
          1. 01Diagnose

            Baseline research, data gathering and stakeholder engagement before any physical work begins: listening to residents and businesses, urban analytics and geospatial mapping, safety audits, and cultural and social asset mapping.

            You are here — this portal is a diagnostic
          2. 02Design

            Evidence translated into masterplans and policy. Planners work alongside communities in design charrettes to co-design solutions that carry nature-based climate resilience, social inclusion and culture-led economic growth, not just architecture.

          3. 03Deliver

            Execution through targeted interventions and funding. Bottom-up seed grants that let communities make their own improvements, and delivery partnerships with municipalities, private enterprise and NGOs for adaptive reuse and infrastructure.

          4. 04Demonstrate

            Testing, validating and showing the result. Small high-impact pilots that prove a concept before it is scaled, then impact tracking against the SDGs and institutionalising what worked into long-term municipal frameworks.

          Method and data provenance

          How the score is built

          Every indicator is winsorised at the 2nd and 98th percentile, min-max normalised to 0–1 across all 160 districts, and direction-corrected so that 1 always means more resilient.

          Within each domain, capacity and vulnerability indicators are averaged separately and never pooled, then combined by geometric mean. The three core domains are combined the same way. Pooling them in an earlier cut let development level dominate: the index correlated +0.62 with population density, and almost all of that came from the capacity side.

          Districts are keyed on the DOSM code_state_district, the official daerah identifier. All three source workbooks join to it at 160 of 160.

          What changed at v1.0

          Retired. District GDP and median household income — development levels rather than resilience capacities, correlating +0.72 and +0.66 with population density. HDI, the Happiness Index and the Gender Gap Index — single state values repeated across every district, all three on the capacity side. The state recycling rate, which was never climate adaptive capacity.

          Added. Three Economic indicators from the Household Income Survey 2022 and 2024: annualised median income growth, the income-to-expenditure ratio and the absolute poverty rate. This lifts Economic vulnerability from one indicator to three, which was the framework's sharpest structural weakness. Five Climate exposure measures from 42 Meteorological Department stations, and a Climate capacity side of three — crop diversity, gazetted forest reserve and the treated-water reserve margin.

          Rank correlation with v0.9.2 is +0.89. The largest single move is Tawau, 124 to 46, which corrects a real defect: its v0.9.2 Economic vulnerability score rested on unemployment alone.

          Known limits

          • Indicators marked STATE are state values repeated across every district in that state. Five of the 40 in the index remain: approved investments, energy resilience, non-revenue water, gazetted forest reserve and treated-water reserve margin.
          • Economic is still 7 capacity indicators to 3 vulnerability. Social runs the other way at 4 to 6. Across the four domains the split is 20 capacity to 20 vulnerability.
          • The index correlates +0.62 with population density, effectively unchanged after the v1.0 retirements. The source has moved: Physical now carries it at +0.68, because piped water, electricity and waste collection are genuinely denser where people are. Social has turned rural-favouring at −0.29. Capacity and vulnerability correlate with each other at only +0.29, so the two halves still measure different things.
          • The 2024 income survey renames six districts and adds six new Sarawak and Sabah daerah that do not exist on the 2020 DOSM spine. Income growth is therefore missing for Perlis and the three Federal Territories.
          • Climate blends the three nearest weather stations by inverse-square distance. The median district sits 34 km from its nearest station, but Belaga is 152 km away and interior Sabah and Sarawak are thinly covered.

          About this dataset

          The Demographic Profile compiles district-level population, ethnicity, vital statistics and income indicators from DOSM’s official publications. It is designed as a companion layer to the Resilient Places Index, giving planners the socioeconomic context behind a district’s resilience score.

          All 160 districts use the same DOSM code_state_district key as the RPI, so every demographic indicator aligns one-to-one with the resilience framework.

          Data sources and reference years

          Population and ethnicity. Population and Housing Census 2020 (DOSM), providing total population, age-sex structure, dependency ratio, ageing index and ethnic composition at district level.

          Vital statistics. Life expectancy at birth (state-level, 2023), crude birth and death rates (state-level, 2023) and rate of natural increase, all from DOSM Vital Statistics publications via data.gov.my. Life expectancy is reported at state level and repeated for every district in that state.

          Income and poverty. Household Income Survey 2022 (DOSM): mean and median household income, Gini coefficient, and absolute and relative poverty incidence at district level. The 2024 survey update is used where available for the RPI’s income growth indicator but not yet reflected in this demographic layer.

          How indicators are mapped

          Each demographic indicator is mapped to a five-class colour ramp using Jenks natural breaks computed across all 160 districts. Indicators where a higher value signals a worse outcome (dependency ratio, ageing index, death rate, Gini, poverty rates, elderly share, non-citizen share) have their colour direction reversed so that darker shading always signals the end of the scale that warrants attention.

          State-level values (life expectancy, birth rate, death rate, natural increase) are repeated across every district in that state. These are marked in the detail panel but not flagged separately in the choropleth.

          Known limits

          • Population data is from the 2020 Census. Post-pandemic migration and new administrative boundaries in Sabah and Sarawak mean some district populations will have shifted materially by now.
          • Vital statistics (life expectancy, birth and death rates) are available only at state level and are repeated for every district in that state, masking within-state variation.
          • Income indicators are from HIS 2022. The 2024 survey renames six districts and adds six new Sarawak and Sabah daerah that do not exist on the 2020 DOSM spine; these are not yet reconciled here.
          • Ethnicity categories follow DOSM’s classification: Malay, Chinese, Indian, Other Bumiputera and Non-Citizen. “Other” (including Orang Asli communities) is folded into “Other Bumiputera” in line with the Census.
          Sources: DOSM district boundaries and codes (dosm-malaysia/data-open); mukim boundaries from geoBoundaries MYS ADM3 (wmgeolab/geoBoundaries, simplified); Social, Economic and Physical indicator workbooks, Resilient Places Index SharePoint folder; Natural Earth 10m coastline; DOSM Household Income Survey 2022 and 2024, and Malaysian Meteorological Department station records 2013–22, both via data.gov.my. Scores are indicative and unvalidated; not for external circulation.
